recovery.retained_file_note: Retained file counts were 76 at baseline, 103 after failure and 129 after recovery. Recovery left one extra empty, unreferenced Parquet file in each Silver directory; neither is part of the active Delta snapshot. Both were checked for zero rows and preserved without cleanup. Silver versions and logical row fingerprints stayed unchanged during recovery.

verification_method: Fresh version-pinned native Spark reads before and after recovery verified every current table, historical rows/counts, schema, event/current-key uniqueness, audit and revenue. Independent OneLake reads reconstructed Delta actions, counted physical rows minus deletion-vector cardinalities, decoded unmasked audit/Gold/event rows and compared complete retained filename/size/SHA-256 manifests. All source bytes were compared with repository fixtures.
deletion_vector_note: The direct OneLake reader does not select exact logical rows from partially masked files. Native Spark verifies those logical rows; independent evidence checks deletion-vector cardinalities and retains all physical data/log/vector files unchanged from earlier snapshots.
limitations: Delta transactions are atomic per table only; Bronze/Silver and a failed audit attempt persisted while Gold was still stale.
One writer per output root is required. Audit guards are not a distributed lock.

The alternate fabric/run_batch.py entry point remains unsupported with the unchanged v0.1.0 wheel when delta-spark distribution metadata is absent. Its guard was reproduced failing closed locally; the verified notebook calls run_pipeline with the managed Spark session. No runtime package was installed or overridden.
